revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Captain Vega's Four Clues
revealWordProblem.text: Captain Vega's expanded treasure map uses base camp at the origin (0, 0). Her four clues are at A(4, 3), B(-5, 2), C(-3, -4), and D(2, -5), where the x-coordinate is units east (+) or west (-) and the y-coordinate is units north (+) or south (-). Question: In which quadrant does each clue land, and how do the signs of its coordinates tell you that without plotting?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: A(4, 3) is in Quadrant I because both coordinates are positive (+, +) — east and north. B(-5, 2) is in Quadrant II because x is negative and y is positive (-, +) — west and north. C(-3, -4) is in Quadrant III because both are negative (-, -) — west and south. D(2, -5) is in Quadrant IV because x is positive and y is negative (+, -) — east and south.

conceptIntro.heading: How do you plot points in all four quadrants?
conceptIntro.intro: The coordinate plane has four parts called quadrants. A negative coordinate means you move left (for x) or down (for y) from the origin instead of right or up.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: The signs of (x, y) tell you the quadrant: (+,+) is I, (-,+) is II, (-,-) is III, (+,-) is IV.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I will plot (-3, -4). I start at the origin (0, 0).
The x is -3, which is negative, so I move 3 units to the LEFT.
The y is -4, which is negative, so I move 4 units DOWN. I place my dot.
Both coordinates are negative, so the point is in Quadrant III.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now let's plot (-5, 2). The x is -5, so which way do we move? Left 5 units.
The y is 2, which is positive, so which way? Up 2 units.
Left and up lands us in which quadrant? Quadrant II.

Picture where Quadrant II sits relative to the origin, then read off the horizontal and vertical directions.
Quadrant II is above the x-axis, so y is positive. Decide what sign x must have for a point on the left side of the plane.
hintsEs: Los cuadrantes se numeran en sentido contrario a las manecillas del reloj, empezando por la esquina superior derecha.
Imagina dónde queda el cuadrante II respecto al origen y después identifica las direcciones horizontal y vertical.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — The Misfired Shot

workedExample.label: Target
workedExample.work: An enemy ship is at (-3, 4). In which quadrant should Captain Vega fire?

workedExample.label: Gunner's thinking
workedExample.work: Ignore the signs and just use the numbers 3 and 4. Both numbers are there, so it must be a bottom-left target.

optional.correctWork: You cannot ignore the signs! The x is -3 (negative = left) and the y is 4 (positive = up). Left and up is Quadrant II, not Quadrant III. Captain Vega should fire on Quadrant II.
hints: Look at the SIGN of each coordinate, not just the number. What does a negative x mean — left or right?
A negative x and a positive y point you left and up. Which quadrant is in the top-left of the map?
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: el disparo fallido
optional.explanation: Ignoring the signs throws away the only information that names a quadrant. With x = -3 the ship is 3 units to the left, and with y = 4 it is 4 units up, which is the top-left region. Left and up is Quadrant II, so firing on Quadrant III would miss entirely.
optional.explanationEs: Ignorar los signos descarta la única información que indica el cuadrante. Con x = -3 la nave está 3 unidades a la izquierda, y con y = 4 está 4 unidades hacia arriba, o sea la región superior izquierda. Izquierda y arriba es el Cuadrante II, así que disparar al Cuadrante III fallaría por completo.

approaching.stem: In which quadrant is the point (-4, 5)?
approaching.explanation: The x-coordinate is negative (left) and the y-coordinate is positive (up). Left and up is Quadrant II.
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
Quadrant III holds points where both coordinates are negative. Here the y-coordinate is 5, which is positive.
Quadrant IV pairs a positive x with a negative y. Look again at the sign of the x-coordinate in (-4, 5).
hints: Look at the signs: x = -4 is negative and y = 5 is positive.
Negative x means move LEFT; positive y means move UP. Ask which corner of the plane is left-and-up.
From the origin, slide left 4 and climb up 5. Quadrants count I, II, III, IV counterclockwise from top-right.
approaching.explanationEs: La coordenada x es negativa (izquierda) y la coordenada y es positiva (arriba). Izquierda y arriba es el cuadrante II.
hintsEs: Mira los signos: x = −4 es negativo y y = 5 es positivo.
Una x negativa significa moverse a la IZQUIERDA; una y positiva significa moverse hacia ARRIBA. Pregunta qué esquina del plano es izquierda y arriba.
Desde el origen, deslízate 4 a la izquierda y sube 5. Los cuadrantes se cuentan I, II, III, IV en sentido antihorario desde arriba a la derecha.

approaching.stem: A point has a positive x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate. Which quadrant is it in?
approaching.explanation: Positive x (right) and negative y (down) = Quadrant IV (bottom-right).
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
Quadrant II needs a negative x-coordinate. This point's x is positive, so it sits on the right side of the plane.
In Quadrant III both coordinates are negative, but only the y-coordinate is negative here.
hints: Positive x pushes you RIGHT; negative y drops you DOWN.
Find the corner that is right of the y-axis and below the x-axis. Quadrants I–IV go counterclockwise from top-right.
Try a sample point like (3, -2): go right 3, then down 2. See which corner of the grid that lands in.
approaching.stemEs: Un punto tiene la coordenada x positiva y la coordenada y negativa. ¿En qué cuadrante está?
approaching.explanationEs: x positiva (derecha) y y negativa (abajo) = cuadrante IV (abajo a la derecha).
hintsEs: Una x positiva te lleva a la DERECHA; una y negativa te baja.
Halla la esquina que está a la derecha del eje y y debajo del eje x. Los cuadrantes I–IV van en sentido antihorario desde arriba a la derecha.
Prueba un punto de ejemplo como (3, −2): ve 3 a la derecha y luego 2 hacia abajo. Mira en qué esquina de la cuadrícula cae.

approaching.stem: Which point is located on the x-axis?
approaching.explanation: A point is on the x-axis when its y-coordinate is 0. (4, 0) is on the x-axis.
choiceFeedback: You swapped the x and y—the first number is horizontal, second is vertical.
Neither coordinate is 0, so this point sits inside a quadrant rather than on an axis. A point on an axis has a coordinate of 0.
Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
hints: A point ON the x-axis never moves up or down — its height is zero.
Check each pair's y-coordinate (the second number). On the x-axis, the y must be 0.
Test (4, 0): right 4, up 0 — do you ever leave the horizontal axis? Now compare with (0, 4).
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál punto está ubicado sobre el eje x?
approaching.explanationEs: Un punto está sobre el eje x cuando su coordenada y es 0. (4, 0) está sobre el eje x.

approaching.label: Match each ordered pair to its quadrant.
approaching.hint: Try the first step of the solution process.
hints: Only the SIGNS matter: (+, +), (-, +), (-, -), and (+, -) each belong to one quadrant.
Use the sign map: I = (+, +), II = (-, +), III = (-, -), IV = (+, -). Read each pair's signs and look them up.
Start with (3, 4): both positive, so Quadrant I. Now read the signs of (-2, 5) and use the map.
approaching.explanation: The signs alone decide the quadrant: (+, +) is I, (-, +) is II, (-, -) is III, and (+, -) is IV. So (3, 4) is Quadrant I, (-2, 5) and (-4, 2) are both Quadrant II, (-6, -1) is Quadrant III, and (1, -3) and (5, -6) are Quadrant IV. How big the numbers are never matters — only whether each one is positive or negative.
approaching.explanationEs: Solo los signos deciden el cuadrante: (+, +) es I, (-, +) es II, (-, -) es III y (+, -) es IV. Así, (3, 4) está en el Cuadrante I, (-2, 5) y (-4, 2) están en el Cuadrante II, (-6, -1) está en el Cuadrante III, y (1, -3) y (5, -6) están en el Cuadrante IV. El tamaño de los números nunca importa, solo si cada uno es positivo o negativo.
approaching.labelEs: Une cada par ordenado con su cuadrante.
hintsEs: Solo importan los SIGNOS: (+, +), (−, +), (−, −) y (+, −) pertenecen cada uno a un cuadrante.
Usa el mapa de signos: I = (+, +), II = (−, +), III = (−, −), IV = (+, −). Lee los signos de cada par y búscalos.
Empieza con (3, 4): ambos positivos, así que Cuadrante I. Ahora lee los signos de (−2, 5) y usa el mapa.

approaching.label: Sort these points by their quadrant: I first, then II, III, IV.
approaching.hint: Arrange items step by step from first to last.
hints: Each card already names its quadrant after the arrow — you're grouping them in order I, II, III, IV.
Collect the Quadrant I cards first, then II, then III, then IV, keeping each group together.
Find the two cards ending in 'I' and place them first. Then look for the card marked 'II'.
approaching.explanation: Each card already shows its quadrant, so the task is grouping them in the order I, II, III, IV. Quadrant I holds (5, 1) and (4, 3) because both coordinates are positive; (-1, 4) is the only Quadrant II card; (-3, -2) and (-5, -7) are Quadrant III with both coordinates negative; and (2, -6) is Quadrant IV.
approaching.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta ya muestra su cuadrante, así que la tarea es agruparlas en el orden I, II, III, IV. El Cuadrante I tiene (5, 1) y (4, 3) porque las dos coordenadas son positivas; (-1, 4) es la única tarjeta del Cuadrante II; (-3, -2) y (-5, -7) son del Cuadrante III con las dos coordenadas negativas; y (2, -6) es del Cuadrante IV.
approaching.labelEs: Clasifica estos puntos por su cuadrante: primero I, después II, III, IV.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta ya nombra su cuadrante después de la flecha: solo las estás agrupando en orden I, II, III, IV.
Reúne primero las tarjetas del Cuadrante I, luego las del II, luego las del III y luego las del IV, manteniendo cada grupo junto.
Halla las dos tarjetas que terminan en 'I' y colócalas primero. Luego busca la tarjeta marcada 'II'.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Name the quadrant for the point (-2, 5).

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: The x is -2, so I move 2 units DOWN. The y is 5, so I move 5 units to the RIGHT.

approaching.correctWork: The signs were matched to the wrong axis. A negative x moves LEFT (not down), and a positive y moves UP (not right). So move 2 units LEFT and 5 units UP. Left and up is Quadrant II, not Quadrant IV.
hints: Which coordinate controls left/right, and which controls up/down? The x is always the left/right move.
x is -2 (negative → left) and y is 5 (positive → up). Left and up land you in which quadrant?
approaching.explanation: The signs were matched to the wrong directions: x controls left and right, and y controls up and down. Since x = -2 you move 2 units LEFT, and since y = 5 you move 5 units UP. Left and up is the top-left region, so the point lands in Quadrant II, not Quadrant IV.
approaching.explanationEs: Los signos se asignaron a las direcciones equivocadas: x controla izquierda y derecha, y y controla arriba y abajo. Como x = -2, te mueves 2 unidades a la IZQUIERDA, y como y = 5, te mueves 5 unidades hacia ARRIBA. Izquierda y arriba es la región superior izquierda, así que el punto cae en el Cuadrante II, no en el Cuadrante IV.

onLevel.label: Plot one point in each quadrant: (3, 2), (-4, 1), (-2, -3), (5, -4)
onLevel.hint: Plot each point by moving right first, then up from the origin.
hints: Signs steer you: positive x goes right, negative x goes left, positive y goes up, negative y goes down.
For each point, do the x move first (left/right), then the y move (up/down). The label tells you which quadrant to expect.
Plot (3, 2) first: right 3, up 2 — the top-right region. Then (-4, 1): LEFT 4, then up 1.
onLevel.explanation: Each point starts at the origin, moves along x first and then along y, and the pair of signs tells you which region you end in. (3, 2) goes right and up to Quadrant I, (-4, 1) goes left and up to Quadrant II, (-2, -3) goes left and down to Quadrant III, and (5, -4) goes right and down to Quadrant IV.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada punto empieza en el origen, se mueve primero en x y luego en y, y la pareja de signos te dice en qué región terminas. (3, 2) va a la derecha y hacia arriba, al Cuadrante I; (-4, 1) va a la izquierda y hacia arriba, al Cuadrante II; (-2, -3) va a la izquierda y hacia abajo, al Cuadrante III; y (5, -4) va a la derecha y hacia abajo, al Cuadrante IV.

onLevel.instructions: For each ordered pair, write the signs of x and y and name the quadrant (or axis).
onLevel.hint: For each point, write the sign of x and y, then name the quadrant or axis.
hints: Each row asks for the sign of x, the sign of y, then the quadrant those signs give — or an axis if a coordinate is 0.
Sign map: (+, +) I, (-, +) II, (-, -) III, (+, -) IV. A 0 for x means y-axis; a 0 for y means x-axis.
Row 1: decide if 6 is positive or negative, then -2. Write both signs, then look the pair up on the sign map.
onLevel.explanation: Write each coordinate's sign, then read the pair off the map: (6, -2) is (+, -) so Quadrant IV, (-3, -5) is (-, -) so Quadrant III, and (-1, 8) is (-, +) so Quadrant II. A zero means the point sits on an axis instead of inside a quadrant — (0, 7) is on the y-axis and (4, 0) is on the x-axis.
onLevel.explanationEs: Escribe el signo de cada coordenada y luego busca la pareja en el mapa: (6, -2) es (+, -), así que Cuadrante IV; (-3, -5) es (-, -), así que Cuadrante III; y (-1, 8) es (-, +), así que Cuadrante II. Un cero significa que el punto está sobre un eje y no dentro de un cuadrante: (0, 7) está en el eje y y (4, 0) está en el eje x.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Para cada par ordenado, escribe los signos de x y y, y nombra el cuadrante (o el eje).
hintsEs: Cada fila pide el signo de x, el signo de y y luego el cuadrante que dan esos signos, o un eje si una coordenada es 0.
Mapa de signos: (+, +) I, (−, +) II, (−, −) III, (+, −) IV. Un 0 en x significa eje y; un 0 en y significa eje x.
Fila 1: decide si 6 es positivo o negativo y luego −2. Escribe ambos signos y luego busca la pareja en el mapa de signos.

onLevel.label: Match each quadrant to its coordinate sign pattern.
onLevel.hint: Try the first step of the solution process.
hints: Quadrants are numbered counterclockwise starting at the top-right.
Picture each region: top-right is right-and-up, top-left is left-and-up. Right/left is x's sign; up/down is y's sign.
Quadrant I is the top-right region: x goes right and y goes up. Which sign pattern says 'both positive'?
onLevel.explanation: Quadrants are numbered counterclockwise from the top-right, so Quadrant I is (+, +), Quadrant II is (-, +), Quadrant III is (-, -), and Quadrant IV is (+, -). The two axis cards work differently: a point on the x-axis has no vertical move, so y = 0, and a point on the y-axis has no horizontal move, so x = 0.
onLevel.explanationEs: Los cuadrantes se numeran en sentido contrario a las manecillas del reloj empezando arriba a la derecha, así que el Cuadrante I es (+, +), el II es (-, +), el III es (-, -) y el IV es (+, -). Las dos tarjetas de ejes funcionan distinto: un punto sobre el eje x no tiene movimiento vertical, así que y = 0, y un punto sobre el eje y no tiene movimiento horizontal, así que x = 0.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada cuadrante con su patrón de signos de coordenadas.
hintsEs: Los cuadrantes se numeran en sentido antihorario empezando arriba a la derecha.
Imagina cada región: arriba a la derecha es derecha y arriba; arriba a la izquierda es izquierda y arriba. Derecha/izquierda es el signo de x; arriba/abajo es el de y.
El Cuadrante I es la región de arriba a la derecha: x va a la derecha y y va hacia arriba. ¿Qué patrón de signos dice 'ambos positivos'?

onLevel.stem: Point A is at (-5, 3). If you move 8 units to the right, what are the new coordinates?
onLevel.explanation: Moving right means adding to the x-coordinate: -5 + 8 = 3. The y stays the same. New point: (3, 3).
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
Remember the x-coordinate tells you how far horizontally.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
hints: Moving right changes ONLY the x-coordinate. The y-coordinate stays at 3.
Add the move to the x-value: take -5 and count up 8. Careful crossing zero — use a number line if it helps.
Start at -5 and count 8 steps right: -4, -3, -2, ... keep going all 8 steps. Then keep the y as 3.
onLevel.stemEs: El punto A está en (-5, 3). Si te mueves 8 unidades a la derecha, ¿cuáles son las nuevas coordenadas?
onLevel.explanationEs: Moverse a la derecha significa sumar a la coordenada x: -5 + 8 = 3. La y se queda igual. Punto nuevo: (3, 3).
hintsEs: Moverse a la derecha cambia SOLO la coordenada x. La coordenada y se queda en 3.
Suma el movimiento al valor de x: toma −5 y cuenta 8 hacia arriba. Cuidado al cruzar el cero; usa una recta numérica si ayuda.
Empieza en −5 y cuenta 8 pasos a la derecha: −4, −3, −2, … sigue los 8 pasos. Luego conserva la y como 3.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Name the quadrant for the point (6, -1).

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: I'll read the coordinates as (y, x), so I treat this like (-1, 6): the first number -1 is negative (left) and the second number 6 is positive (up).

onLevel.correctWork: The order was reversed. In an ordered pair (x, y), x ALWAYS comes first. Here x = 6 (positive → right) and y = -1 (negative → down). Right and down is Quadrant IV, not Quadrant II.
hints: In (6, -1), which number is the x-coordinate — the first or the second?
x = 6 (positive → right) and y = -1 (negative → down). Right and down land you in which quadrant?
onLevel.explanation: An ordered pair is always (x, y), so the first number is the horizontal move and the order cannot be swapped. Here x = 6 sends you right and y = -1 sends you down, which is the bottom-right region — Quadrant IV. Reading it as (-1, 6) described a completely different point.
onLevel.explanationEs: Un par ordenado siempre es (x, y), así que el primer número es el movimiento horizontal y el orden no se puede intercambiar. Aquí x = 6 te manda a la derecha y y = -1 te manda hacia abajo, que es la región inferior derecha: el Cuadrante IV. Leerlo como (-1, 6) describía un punto completamente distinto.

onLevel.stem: In which quadrant is the point (-3, 5)?
onLevel.explanation: Negative x with positive y places the point in Quadrant II.
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
Quadrant III requires both coordinates to be negative, but 5 is positive.
Quadrant IV needs a positive x-coordinate, and here x is −3.
hints: Check the signs: x = -3 is negative and y = 5 is positive.
Negative x means left of the y-axis; positive y means above the x-axis. Which quadrant is up-and-left?
From the origin move left 3, then up 5. Count quadrants counterclockwise from top-right to name where you land.
onLevel.explanationEs: Una x negativa con una y positiva coloca el punto en el cuadrante II.
hintsEs: Revisa los signos: x = −3 es negativo y y = 5 es positivo.
Una x negativa significa a la izquierda del eje y; una y positiva significa arriba del eje x. ¿Qué cuadrante es arriba y a la izquierda?
Desde el origen muévete 3 a la izquierda y luego 5 hacia arriba. Cuenta los cuadrantes en sentido antihorario desde arriba a la derecha para nombrar dónde caes.

onLevel.stem: What are the coordinates of a point 4 units right and 2 units down from the origin?
onLevel.explanation: Right is +x and down is -y, so the point is (4, -2).
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
The two coordinates are swapped. The first number always describes the horizontal move and the second the vertical move.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
hints: Two moves: right 4 (horizontal) and down 2 (vertical). Down means a NEGATIVE y.
Build (x, y): x is the right/left amount with its sign, y is the up/down amount with its sign.
Right 4 gives x = 4 (positive). Now write 'down 2' as a signed y-value and put the two in order.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Cuáles son las coordenadas de un punto que está 4 unidades a la derecha y 2 unidades hacia abajo desde el origen?
onLevel.explanationEs: A la derecha es +x y hacia abajo es -y, así que el punto es (4, -2).
hintsEs: Dos movimientos: derecha 4 (horizontal) y abajo 2 (vertical). Abajo significa una y NEGATIVA.
Arma (x, y): x es la cantidad derecha/izquierda con su signo y y es la cantidad arriba/abajo con su signo.
Derecha 4 da x = 4 (positivo). Ahora escribe 'abajo 2' como un valor de y con signo y pon los dos en orden.

extending.title: Find the Quadrant Error

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: The x is -3, so I go left 3. The y is -5, so I go up 5.

extending.correctWork: A negative y-coordinate means DOWN, not up. Go left 3 and DOWN 5. The point (-3, -5) is in Quadrant III (both negative), not Quadrant II.
hints: What direction does a NEGATIVE y-coordinate go — up or down?
Both coordinates are negative. In which quadrant are both x and y negative?
extending.explanation: A negative y-coordinate means down, not up. From the origin you go left 3 and DOWN 5, landing in the bottom-left region. Both coordinates are negative, and (-, -) is Quadrant III, not Quadrant II.
extending.explanationEs: Una coordenada y negativa significa hacia abajo, no hacia arriba. Desde el origen te mueves 3 a la izquierda y 5 hacia ABAJO, y caes en la región inferior izquierda. Las dos coordenadas son negativas, y (-, -) es el Cuadrante III, no el Cuadrante II.

extending.prompt: A point starts in Quadrant I at (4, 6). Describe a move that puts it in Quadrant III. What must happen to both coordinates? Can you give the exact new coordinates after your move?
extending.sentenceFrame: To move from Quadrant I to Quadrant III, both coordinates must become ___. Starting at (4, 6), I could move ___ units left and ___ units down to reach (___,___), which is in Quadrant III because ___.
extending.hint: Use examples with specific coordinates to explain your thinking.
hints: Quadrant III is the bottom-left region — think about what must be true of BOTH signs there.
Plan moves that flip each sign: enough LEFT to push x = 4 below zero, enough DOWN to push y = 6 below zero.
Try moving left MORE than 4 units — say how far x = 4 travels and where it lands. Then plan the down move for y = 6.
extending.explanation: Quadrant III is the bottom-left region, so both coordinates have to end up negative. Starting at (4, 6), you need to move more than 4 units left to push x below 0 and more than 6 units down to push y below 0. Moving 6 left and 8 down, for example, lands on (-2, -2), which is Quadrant III because x and y are both negative.
extending.explanationEs: El Cuadrante III es la región inferior izquierda, así que las dos coordenadas deben terminar negativas. Empezando en (4, 6), necesitas moverte más de 4 unidades a la izquierda para llevar x por debajo de 0 y más de 6 unidades hacia abajo para llevar y por debajo de 0. Por ejemplo, moverte 6 a la izquierda y 8 hacia abajo cae en (-2, -2), que está en el Cuadrante III porque x y y son negativas.
extending.promptEs: Un punto empieza en el cuadrante I en (4, 6). Describe un movimiento que lo lleve al cuadrante III. ¿Qué debe pasar con las dos coordenadas? ¿Puedes dar las coordenadas nuevas exactas después de tu movimiento?
hintsEs: El Cuadrante III es la región de abajo a la izquierda: piensa qué debe cumplirse con AMBOS signos ahí.
Planea movimientos que cambien cada signo: suficiente IZQUIERDA para que x = 4 baje de cero y suficiente ABAJO para que y = 6 baje de cero.
Prueba moverte MÁS de 4 unidades a la izquierda: di cuánto viaja x = 4 y dónde cae. Luego planea el movimiento hacia abajo para y = 6.

extending.label: Plot these 4 points and connect them in order to form a shape. Name the shape and identify which quadrants it spans: (-3, 2), (3, 2), (3, -2), (-3, -2)
extending.hint: Start at the origin (0, 0) for each point. Move right first, then up.
hints: Signs steer each plot. Notice the points reuse 3s and 2s with different signs — that symmetry builds the shape.
Plot in order A, B, C, D and connect as you go. Then check which of the four quadrants each corner sits in.
Plot A(-3, 2) first: left 3, up 2 — the top-left region. Then B(3, 2): right 3, up 2.
extending.explanation: The four points reuse 3 and 2 with different signs, so connecting A(-3, 2), B(3, 2), C(3, -2), D(-3, -2) in order draws a rectangle 6 units wide and 4 units tall centered on the origin. One corner sits in each region — A in Quadrant II, B in Quadrant I, C in Quadrant IV, and D in Quadrant III — so the shape spans all four quadrants.
extending.explanationEs: Los cuatro puntos reutilizan el 3 y el 2 con signos distintos, así que conectar A(-3, 2), B(3, 2), C(3, -2), D(-3, -2) en orden dibuja un rectángulo de 6 unidades de ancho y 4 de alto centrado en el origen. Cada esquina cae en una región distinta: A en el Cuadrante II, B en el I, C en el IV y D en el III, así que la figura abarca los cuatro cuadrantes.

extending.stem: A point (a, b) has a < 0 and b < 0. In which quadrant does it lie?
extending.explanation: Both coordinates negative places the point in Quadrant III.
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
Quadrant II has a negative x but a positive y, and here b is negative too.
Quadrant IV pairs a positive x with a negative y, but a is negative here.
hints: a < 0 means the x is negative; b < 0 means the y is negative — this is a signs question in disguise.
Negative x goes left and negative y goes down. Find the down-and-left region, counting I–IV counterclockwise.
Pick a sample like (-2, -3) and plot it: left 2, down 3. Which region did you land in?
extending.stemEs: Un punto (a, b) tiene a < 0 y b < 0. ¿En qué cuadrante se encuentra?
extending.explanationEs: Tener las dos coordenadas negativas coloca el punto en el cuadrante III.

extending.stem: Reflecting the point (3, -6) across the x-axis gives which point?
extending.explanation: Reflecting across the x-axis negates the y-coordinate: (3, -6) → (3, 6).
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.
Both coordinates changed sign, which is a reflection across both axes. A reflection across the x-axis leaves the x-coordinate alone.
You swapped the x and y—the first number is horizontal, second is vertical.
hints: Reflecting across the x-axis flips a point vertically — up/down changes, left/right doesn't.
The x-coordinate stays the same; the y-coordinate switches sign. Don't swap the order of the two numbers.
Keep the 3. The point sits 6 below the x-axis, so its mirror sits the same 6 units ABOVE. Build that pair.
extending.stemEs: Reflejar el punto (3, -6) sobre el eje x da como resultado ¿cuál punto?
extending.explanationEs: Reflejar sobre el eje x cambia el signo de la coordenada y: (3, -6) → (3, 6).
hintsEs: Reflejar sobre el eje x voltea el punto verticalmente: cambia arriba/abajo, no izquierda/derecha.
La coordenada x se queda igual; la coordenada y cambia de signo. No intercambies el orden de los dos números.
Conserva el 3. El punto está 6 debajo del eje x, así que su reflejo está esas mismas 6 unidades ARRIBA. Arma ese par.

optionalActivity.name: Four-Quadrant Battleship
optionalActivity.intro: Captain Vega's fleet is hidden across all four quadrants of the treasure map — call out the coordinates to land each shot!

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants is matching each sign to the wrong axis — for example, seeing (-2, 5) and thinking "the x is negative so I move DOWN, and the y is positive so I move RIGHT," which lands the point in Quadrant IV. But the x-coordinate always controls left/right, never up/down: negative x means LEFT (not down), and positive y means UP (not right). So (-2, 5) is actually left 2, up 5 — Quadrant II. Before you submit, check that you used the x-coordinate for left/right and the y-coordinate for up/down, and never swapped them.

diagram.title: City Map: Four-Quadrant Locations
diagram.caption: City Hall sits at the origin; read each point's signs to see its quadrant — Library (-,+) is II, School (+,+) is I, Park (+,-) is IV, Hospital (-,-) is III.

connect.scenario: A city uses a coordinate grid to map locations. City Hall is at the origin (0, 0). The library is at (-3, 4), the park is at (5, -2), the school is at (2, 3), and the hospital is at (-4, -1).
connect.promptQuestion: How do four-quadrant coordinates help a city map locations in every direction from the center?
connect.prompt: The library is in Quadrant ___ because its x is ___ and its y is ___. The park is in Quadrant ___ because ___. Four-quadrant coordinates help because ___.

check.stem: Which quadrant is the library (−3, 4) in?
check.explanation: x is negative (left of center) and y is positive (above center). That is the upper-left region — Quadrant II.

check.stem: Which quadrant is the park (5, −2) in?
check.explanation: x is positive (right) and y is negative (below). That is the lower-right region — Quadrant IV.

check.stem: Which location is in Quadrant III?
check.explanation: Quadrant III is where BOTH coordinates are negative — the lower-left region. The hospital at (−4, −1) is the only one.

connect.modelAnswer: Read the signs to find the quadrant. Library (−3, 4): x negative, y positive → Quadrant II. Park (5, −2): x positive, y negative → Quadrant IV. The school (2, 3) is Quadrant I and the hospital (−4, −1) is Quadrant III. Four quadrants let the city map locations in every direction from City Hall at the origin, instead of only up and to the right.

exitTicket.stem: A point has a negative x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate. Which quadrant is it in?
exitTicket.explanation: Quadrant III is where both x and y are negative. This means the point is left of the origin and below the origin.
choiceFeedback: Quadrant I has both positive — you need both negative.
Quadrant II has negative x but positive y — check the y sign.
Quadrant IV has positive x — you need x negative too.
hints: Negative x and negative y — think about which direction each sign pushes the point.
Negative x means LEFT of the y-axis; negative y means BELOW the x-axis. Find the region that is both.
Plot a sample like (-4, -5): left 4, down 5. Count quadrants counterclockwise from top-right to name it.

questions.stem: Where is -3/4 located on the number line?
questions.explanation: -3/4 = -0.75, which is between 0 and -1. It is 3/4 of the way from 0 toward -1.

questions.stem: Which point is located between -1 and -2 on the number line?
questions.explanation: -1.5 is between -1 and -2 because it is 0.5 units to the left of -1 (or 0.5 units to the right of -2).
